name: Linear Atrophoderma of Moulin

criteria.description: Presence of unilateral, linear, hyperpigmented, atrophic plaques following Blaschko lines
Skin biopsy showing epidermal atrophy with normal dermis and absence of sclerosis or inflammation
Exclusion of other linear atrophic dermatoses such as linear morphea or linear scleroderma
No systemic symptoms or internal organ involvement

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria must be met: characteristic clinical presentation, supportive histopathology, and exclusion of other linear atrophic dermatoses
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by histopathology and exclusion of mimics

pathognomonic.symptomName: Unilateral linear hyperpigmented atrophic plaques following Blaschko lines
searchTerms: one-sided linear dark thin skin scars
Blaschko line skin thinning with pigmentation

pathognomonic.symptomName: Absence of induration or sclerosis in affected skin
searchTerms: no hardening or thickening of skin
symptoms starting in childhood or teens

common.symptomName: Mild skin atrophy without significant texture change
common.notes: Atrophy is subtle compared to other atrophic dermatoses
searchTerms: mild skin thinning without texture change
skin looks thinner but normal feel

occasional.symptomName: Mild pruritus localized to affected areas
searchTerms: localized mild itching on affected skin

occasional.symptomName: Slight textural skin changes such as mild thinning
No associated nail or hair abnormalities
searchTerms: no changes in hair or nails
small visible blood vessels in skin
mild skin redness with visible vessels

rare.symptomName: Slight hypopigmentation adjacent to hyperpigmented plaques
searchTerms: light skin patches near dark spots
lighter skin next to dark plaques
areas of reduced pigmentation beside darker skin
little immune cell presence in skin

imaging: Skin ultrasound may show epidermal thinning
genetic: Etiology possibly mosaicism along Blaschko lines
other: Histopathology: epidermal atrophy without dermal sclerosis or significant inflammation

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of dermal sclerosis and induration
Positive autoimmune serology in some cases
Usually affects cheeks and perioral area

redFlags: Rapid progression of skin induration or sclerosis
Development of systemic symptoms such as joint pain or Raynaud phenomenon
Presence of ulceration or skin breakdown
references: Moulin G. Atrophoderma of Moulin: a linear atrophic dermatosis following Blaschko lines. Dermatologica. 1992.
Laxer RM, Zulian F. Localized scleroderma. Curr Opin Rheumatol. 2006.
Bolognia JL, Schaffer JV, Cerroni L. Dermatology. 4th ed. Elsevier; 2018.
